_comment: Estates: the great orders of the realm. influence: base_influence plus per_share x the share of the people in the estate's occupation, plus its privileges, plus land the crown has let slip; loyalty drifts to 40 plus its privileges' loyalty. loyal (60 and up) and disloyal (under 30) give modifiers (the keys laws and techs use). Privileges are granted and revoked by the crown.

estates.name: The Temples
estates.description: The priesthoods of the great gods: landowners, scholars and the keepers of the king's legitimacy.

privileges.name: Temple estates
privileges.description: The temples hold their lands free of tax.

privileges.name: Temple schools
privileges.description: The temples teach the sons of the great families.

privileges.name: The festival calendar
privileges.description: The crown keeps the feasts of the gods at its own cost.

estates.name: The Nobles
estates.description: The great families, the chariot-owners and the lords of the nomes: they lead the levies and hold the provinces.

privileges.name: Noble command of the levies
privileges.description: The lords lead the regiments of their own lands.

privileges.name: Hereditary offices
privileges.description: Governorships pass from father to son.

privileges.name: Exemption from tribute
privileges.description: The great estates pay no tribute to the crown.

estates.name: The Artisans and Merchants
estates.description: The workshops, the caravan masters and the shipowners of the towns.

privileges.name: Guild charters
privileges.description: The crafts rule their own trades.

privileges.name: Merchant courts
privileges.description: Disputes of trade are judged by the merchants themselves.

privileges.name: Protection of the caravans
privileges.description: The crown guards the roads at its cost.

estates.name: The Scribes
estates.description: The officials, the overseers and the keepers of the accounts: the state's own hands.

privileges.name: Tenure of office
privileges.description: Officials cannot be removed at the king's whim.

privileges.name: The House of Life
privileges.description: A royal school for scribes, at the crown's cost.

privileges.name: Estates for the officials
privileges.description: Land grants to those who serve.
